clue.text: Rejected fish unacceptable for stew

indicators.note: something rejected is turned back, so the fish's name is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
out, as in 'that's out', means not acceptable

explanation.surface: A cook sends back an unpalatable fish, deeming it unfit for the stew pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragout is a highly seasoned French stew of meat and vegetables.

clue.text: Clearance resulting from free ball

parts.note: to rid is to free of something
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A footballer's clearance comes from a free kick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free ball' suggests a free kick; 'ball' is a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting rid of something unwanted is clearing it away, a removal.

clue.text: Abuse one's urge to be magnanimous

indicators.note: to abuse something is to misuse and mangle it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mistreating your desires makes you big-hearted.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnanimous means big-hearted and forgiving, liberal in giving.

clue.text: American editor briefly employed

parts.note: US is short for American, as in US citizen
ED is the short form of editor

explanation.surface: An American editor had a short stint in a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something employed has been put to use, applied or utilised.

clue.text: Pass quickly in striking football kit

parts.note: workers who are striking are out
a team's strip is its football kit

explanation.surface: A footballer races past opponents while wearing an eye-catching kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' reads as 'eye-catching' but means on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip is to overtake or get ahead of, moving faster than a rival.

clue.text: Accepted financial responsibility for being subscribed?

definitions.meaning: guaranteed, as an insurer guarantees a risk
literally sub-scribed: written below, as a signature under a document

explanation.surface: Taking on the cost of something once signed up to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subscribed' is read in its Latin sense: scribed under.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurers guarantee policies; and a name signed at the foot of a document is literally put beneath the text.

clue.text: Twisted point supported by witticism

indicators.note: in a down clue the point sits above, held up by the witticism

parts.note: S is south, a compass point
a pun is a play on words

explanation.surface: A twisted argument propped up by a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarn that is spun has been twisted into thread.

clue.text: Standard textbook for you

definitions.meaning: a basic book for learners, a primer
the person reading this clue

explanation.surface: A recommended school book for the student.
explanation.definitionFit: A primer used in schools has this name, and the person perusing the clue is one too.

clue.text: Flagrant licence

definitions.meaning: blatant, obvious
an official grant of exclusive rights to an invention

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means obvious or blatant; the noun is an exclusive licence for an invention.

clue.text: Assumed academic gets study back

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

indicators.note: back tells us the study's word is read in reverse

parts.note: a den is a private study or room

explanation.surface: A lecturer retreats once more to his study.
explanation.definitionFit: Assumed, as in assumed a robe or garment, means put on clothing.

clue.text: Officer and worker giving backing to commercial project

indicators.note: the worker stands behind, at the back of, the other pieces

parts.note: an ad, or commercial, is an advertisement
to project is to jut out
a worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: An officer and an employee support a business venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commercial project' reads as one business venture; 'project' is a verb here, to stick out.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjutant is a military officer assisting a commander with administration.

clue.text: Demonstrate concern for the entertainment industry

parts.note: to demonstrate is to show
a concern is a business or firm

explanation.surface: Express worry about the state of the entertainment world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concern' reads as worry but means a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: The world of theatre, film and popular performance is commonly known by this phrase.

clue.text: Wary about appearing crooked

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is suspicious of looking dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' reads as dishonest, but means askew.
explanation.definitionFit: Awry means askew, off the straight, so physically bent or twisted.

clue.text: Beguile a lot of finches

definitions.meaning: to beguile is to enchant or captivate
the collective noun for a flock of goldfinches

explanation.surface: Lure in a flock of birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming someone is enchanting them; a gathering of goldfinches is traditionally called by this collective noun.

clue.text: Intend to be parsimonious

definitions.meaning: to intend something is to have it in mind as a purpose
stingy, tight with money

explanation.surface: Plan to be stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is having a purpose in mind; the adjective sense is miserly or stingy.

clue.text: He must be prepared to reconnoitre

definitions.meaning: 'Be Prepared' is the motto of the Boy ... movement
to explore an area to gather information

explanation.surface: Someone must get ready to survey the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Baden-Powell's youth movement's motto is 'Be Prepared'; the verb means to explore ahead for information.

clue.text: Loud, constantly making complaint

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
ever means always, constantly

explanation.surface: Someone complains loudly and endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' suggests a grumble but means an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be an ailment, and a high temperature is one such illness.

clue.text: It gives a long smoke for the parochial representative

definitions.meaning: a long-stemmed clay tobacco pipe bears this name
a lay officer elected by a parish to look after church property

explanation.surface: Something offering a lengthy puff is linked to a parish official.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are one word: a long clay pipe and an Anglican lay parish officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A long clay pipe was named for parish officials; the same word is the elected lay officer of an Anglican parish.

clue.text: Acknowledging nothing has been settled?

definitions.meaning: admitting, granting
if no bill is paid, everything is still owed

explanation.surface: Admitting that no matter has been resolved.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word into ALL OWING: every debt unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Granting or conceding a point is admitting it, the sense of acknowledging.

clue.text: Tormented in San Diego appallingly

indicators.note: appallingly suggests something done badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone suffered terribly in a Californian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in anguish or great pain is to be tormented.

clue.text: One way to raise the standard

definitions.text: One way to raise the standard

parts.words: One way to raise the standard
parts.note: raising standards sounds like improving quality, but here a standard is a flag hoisted up a pole

explanation.surface: A suggestion for improving quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' suggests a level of quality; it is a banner hoisted up a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and hoisting one up a mast is this phrase, also used of floating an idea.

clue.text: Still good advice to the overexcited

definitions.meaning: to still is to make calm or motionless
split as ..., what one tells an agitated person

explanation.surface: Calming words for someone too worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' is a verb, to quieten; the second sense splits the word as BE CALM.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a ship motionless for lack of wind is to still it; the split phrase is a plea for composure.

clue.text: Opera dealing with loveless romance?

indicators.note: dealing, as with cards, implies shuffling, so the letters are mixed
love is zero, the letter O, which is taken away

explanation.surface: An opera about a romance with no love in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' removes O (love, zero in tennis) from ROMANCE, giving RMANCE; 'dealing' shuffles RMANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizet's opera of the gypsy cigarette girl of Seville carries this title.

clue.text: Use a different name for Jacob's twin brother

indicators.note: different asks for the letters to be put in a different order

explanation.surface: Call Jacob's twin by another name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the elder twin of Jacob sold his birthright for a bowl of stew.

clue.text: Going down, he may be saved by the bell

definitions.text: Going down, he may be saved by the bell

parts.words: Going down, he may be saved by the bell
parts.note: sounds like a boxer floored and rescued by the end-of-round bell, but means someone underwater using a diving bell

explanation.surface: A boxer on the canvas is rescued as the round ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxing picture misleads: the bell is a diving bell, an air chamber lowered underwater.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who descends underwater might rely on a diving bell, an open-bottomed chamber holding air.

clue.text: Depressed area of Ulster?

definitions.meaning: feeling low, gloomy
County ... is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A gloomy part of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low is a synonym for gloomy; County Down is a county of Northern Ireland, historically in Ulster.

clue.text: Appropriate to raise a cap here in America

parts.note: U means upper-class, socially acceptable or appropriate

indicators.note: in a down clue raising turns the word upwards, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a cap is a hat

explanation.surface: In America it is polite to doff one's cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' is U, the old label for upper-class, proper usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A western US state, so a place in America, suiting 'here'.

clue.text: Upset servicemen will get leave in consequence

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means overturned, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: Disgruntled troops will be given time off as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' looks like a noun, time off, but is the verb to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for therefore, used to introduce a logical conclusion.

clue.text: Made concession to be allowed in

definitions.meaning: conceded or confessed a point
granted entry

explanation.surface: Someone gave ground in order to gain entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceding a point and being granted entry are both senses of the same past-tense verb.

clue.text: Ditches with water in the middle?

definitions.text: Ditches with water in the middle?

parts.words: Ditches with water in the middle?
parts.note: a ditch with water running along its centre is a channel carrying water away

explanation.surface: Trenches full of water along their centres.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a whimsical description; RAIN, a kind of water, also sits in the middle of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Channels or ditches that carry water away are drainage channels, matching the clue's watery trenches.

clue.text: Home isn't refurbished by the landlord

indicators.note: refurbished means done up anew, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A house left unrenovated by the property owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landlord' suggests a property owner; the answer is a jocular term for a pub's innkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorous, old-fashioned way to address or describe the keeper of an inn or pub.

clue.text: Pursued, being persistent

definitions.meaning: followed closely, tailed
tenacious, refusing to give up

explanation.surface: Chased by someone who refuses to quit.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning tailed or followed closely, and an adjective meaning tenacious.
